svg.title: SLSA v1.2 Build track levels and in-toto provenance architecture
svg.desc: Three panels. The first lists the SLSA v1.2 Build track levels: L0 gives no guarantees, L1 requires provenance to exist and be distributed, L2 requires authentic verifiable provenance from a hosted build platform, and L3 requires a hardened platform where build runs cannot influence one another and platform secrets stay unreachable from user-defined build steps. It also notes that v1.2 approved a Source track alongside Build. The second describes the in-toto provenance predicate fields: builder ID, build type, external parameters and resolved dependencies, and the subject digest. The third panel covers verification and states explicitly that hermetic and reproducible builds are not Build L3 requirements, that SLSA treats network isolation as a future direction, and that SLSA attests how an artifact was built rather than whether its inputs were benign.
svg.text: SLSA & Build Provenance Attestations
SLSA v1.2 Build track levels (L0–L3), in-toto provenance statements, and what build integrity does not cover.
SLSA V1.2 BUILD TRACK LEVELS
Graduated Build Integrity Guarantees
• L0: no build integrity guarantees
• L1: provenance exists and is distributed to consumers
• L2: authentic, verifiable provenance from a hosted platform
• L3: hardened — runs cannot influence one another and
platform secrets stay out of user-defined build steps
• v1.2 also approves a Source track alongside Build
IN-TOTO PROVENANCE SCHEMA
Verifiable Build Attestation Predicate
• Builder ID: the hosted build service making the claim
• BuildType: names the schema the parameters follow
• External parameters and resolved dependencies
(source repository and git commit digest)
• Subject: SHA-256 digest of the output artifact
• Builder ID and buildType are what a policy pins
VERIFICATION, AND WHAT SITS BEYOND BUILD L3
Cryptographic Verification vs Source Code Auditing
• Verification policy: the verifier matches the artifact digest and the builder ID against signed provenance from a trusted builder
• Hermetic and reproducible builds are NOT Build L3 requirements — SLSA treats network isolation as a future direction
• Security limit: SLSA attests *how* an artifact was built; it does not attest that the source or its dependencies were benign
SLSA INTEGRITY FLOW: SOURCE COMMIT → HOSTED BUILDER → SIGNED IN-TOTO ATTESTATION → VERIFIER VALIDATION
